input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets or exceeds the preferred WARRANTY position, so no redline is warranted. §19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike standard performed by qualified personnel to industry standards, plus an untimed warranty that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to documentation and specifications. §19.2 gives 90 days after the later of delivery or acceptance for each Deliverable — and because "Deliverable" under §1.4 is bespoke work product (reports, configurations, integrations, training material) rather than licensed software, 90 days matches our preferred services-side period; the software/hosted element is warranted to conform throughout the whole subscription term, exceeding our 12-month preferred software period. §19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty, and no-functionality-diminution and open-source protections. §19.4 delivers the full preferred remedy stack: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; §6.2 adds acceptance-stage correction and refund rights. §19.5 confirms the disclaimer is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality or data-protection duty, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. The only softening is that the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," which is market-standard and does not undercut the position given the non-exclusive remedies; it is not worth reopening a favourable package. The spelled-out "ninety days" phrasing is legally unambiguous and is a drafting-convention point only, not a substantive shortfall.
